answer: Each identity must bind to a uniquely trained model, like a basalt monument no cheap cast can copy. Training leaves a weight-space fingerprint: near-identical weights expose clones, so a sybil pays full training compute per copy. The fingerprint is published like a relic in a public registry, re-verified by strangers with fine-tuning probes. Standing accrues only to the fingerprint, never to a bare key, so splitting one model across names earns nothing extra. A sonnet of provenance - dataset hashes, logs, checkpoint signatures - makes origins auditable; any weight-copy forfeits the bond.
